{"id": "a7d71aa1-2e12-4af4-851d-690cf28d3217", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Given only those two facts, here's what can and can't be reported for this specific investigation:

**What can be reported:**
- A list/count of this investigation's AWS and third-party tool calls (pulled straight from its journal) — e.g., "N AWS calls, M third-party calls."
- Qualitative attribution: which services/tools this investigation touched.

**What cannot be reported:**
- Any dollar or seconds figure of agent runtime **specifically for this investigation**. The 600 seconds in the AWS/AIDevOps metric is scoped to the whole Agent Space for that day, aggregated across "several investigations and chats" — there's no per-execution breakdown in that metric, and the journal has no billed agent-seconds of its own to fill that gap.
- Any even split of the 600 seconds across investigations would be a fabricated estimate, not a reported fact — attributing time or cost per investigation would require either execution-level agent-seconds in the journal (which don't exist here) or a metric dimensioned by investigation/execution ID (which this metric isn't).

**Bottom line:** the only defensible cost-adjacent artifact for this investigation is its tool-call inventory (a proxy for *activity*, not *cost*). The actual agent-seconds/cost figure is only known at the Agent Space+day granularity, and mixing it into a per-investigation number would require an assumption not present in the supplied facts.

If you want, I can pull this investigation's actual journal to enumerate its tool calls, or look at whether the cost-insights skill has a different metric that's dimensioned per investigation rather than per Agent Space — want me to check either?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
